bull_case: Custom AI accelerators plus Ethernet networking become a durable hyperscale architecture layer while VMware private-cloud software remains a separate cash engine. Multi-generation OpenAI/Meta programs and >20GW XPV deployment support a multi-year demand shift.
bear_case: AI infrastructure spending normalizes, hyperscalers internalize more silicon, and Broadcom's largest customers gain bargaining power. Customer and TSMC concentration can then offset the benefit of having a separate software franchise.
thesis: The structural shift is real and Broadcom is a leader in custom AI silicon and networking rather than a passive beneficiary. Two independently material demand pools—AI semiconductor and infrastructure software—support durability, but customer-owned architectures and extreme concentration prevent a category-defining 90 score.

evidence.claim: Q3 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue was $16.7B, +221% y/y; Q4 AI semiconductor guidance was $21.7B, +236% y/y.
evidence.source: Broadcom Q3 FY2026 official earnings release, 2026-09-02

evidence.claim: RPO was approximately $179.2B at 2026-08-02, including a long-term custom AI accelerator contract; about 25% was expected to be recognized over the next 12 months.
Broadcom announced multi-generation custom-AI programs with OpenAI and Meta; the Meta program combines 2nm custom accelerators with Broadcom Ethernet scale-up/scale-out networking.
evidence.source: Broadcom official OpenAI announcement 2026-06-24 and Meta announcement 2026-04-14

evidence.claim: Broadcom's AI XPV platform was designed to enable more than 20GW of AI compute through 2028, beginning with a $35B transaction for more than 1GW.

Q3 FY2026 revenue mix was 70% semiconductor solutions and 30% infrastructure software; AI semiconductor revenue alone was about 56% of total company revenue, leaving infrastructure software as a separately material demand pool.
evidence.source: User-supplied Q3 FY2026 10-Q plus official Q3 AI revenue disclosure

evidence.claim: One semiconductor distributor represented 50% of Q3 revenue and the top five end customers represented about 55%; approximately 95% of contract-manufactured wafers were produced by TSMC during 9M FY2026.

counterevidence: The customers defining custom-XPU architectures are themselves technically and financially capable of internal silicon development or dual sourcing.
AI XPV demonstrates deployment demand but also shows that some customers need external capital structures to absorb infrastructure.
The top-five end-customer share rose from about 40% in FY2025 to 55% in Q3 FY2026.
TSMC concentration leaves a major supply-side dependency even if end demand remains strong.
unknowns: Long-run share of custom-AI accelerator economics retained by Broadcom versus customers.
Customer-specific AI contract duration, cancellation economics and pricing are undisclosed.
No precise split of non-AI semiconductor end markets is available to prove a third independent >10% final-market bucket.
falsifiers: Structural leadership weakens if AI semiconductor growth falls below 30% while RPO declines for two consecutive quarters.
Category leadership weakens if major customers move two consecutive accelerator generations away from Broadcom.
Durability score falls if infrastructure software drops below 10% of revenue or customer concentration exceeds 65% without offsetting diversification.
next_checks: Track custom-XPU program diversification beyond OpenAI/Meta.
Separate non-AI semiconductor final markets to test whether a third independent >10% demand pool exists.
Monitor TSMC concentration and second-source progress.

subscores.rationale: Multi-generation customer programs, $179.2B RPO and accelerating AI revenue support the 75 long-duration demand/willingness-to-pay anchor. 90 is excluded because the cycle is young and XPV financing plus concentration can amplify normalization.

Broadcom co-designs custom accelerators and supplies the Ethernet fabric for multiple frontier customers, supporting demonstrated leadership. 90 is excluded because customers own important architecture decisions and Broadcom does not unilaterally define the platform standard.

Two independently material demand pools are directly evidenced above 10% of revenue: AI semiconductor and infrastructure software. The table therefore maps to 75. Aggregate non-AI semiconductor revenue is not counted as a third final market because its constituent end-market shares are undisclosed.

uncertainties.rationale: Current AI growth is extraordinary and may include capacity-build timing.
Customer control over architecture limits Broadcom's ability to dictate standards.
Customer and TSMC concentration can correlate otherwise separate demand pools.
